newsitem.title: UK: Japan aluminium market needs wider participation.
newsitem.headline: Japan aluminium market needs wider participation.

text.p: The fledgling Japanese aluminium futures contract, launched earlier this year, needs wider participation and bigger volumes to flourish, Satoshi Hamamoto of Marubeni Corp's Light Metals Department said.
"If the non-participation of the industry, overseas brokers, and the LME brokers continues, it will become a minor market," Hamamoto said at the Financial Times World Aluminium Conference.
Aluminium futures started trading on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) on April 7, with first-day turnover nearly 20,000 lots.

But volumes have slumped and are now around just 1,000 lots daily, which is mostly from private investors. The contract is difficult to use for hedging, and the key to its success will be if it can attract industry use, he said.
"It is still to early to judge it correctly - we have to wait and see until seven months are listed," Hamamoto added.
TOCOM may have to consider extending the trading hours of the contract, which trades on computers between 0900-1100 and 1300-1530 hrs in Japan.
Meanwhile, the Osaka Mercantile Exchange (OME) is also launching an aluminium futures contract in October this year, which will be traded in an open-outcry manner.
"We think that the situation will be very difficult (when it starts)," Hamamoto said.
